**Severity:** error · **Area:** Resume (`RV2xxx`) · **Quick fix:** yes

## Message

The diagnostic reads one of:

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}.{field}`: {Class} instance holds a resource (its field reads `{global}`); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}`: {Class} instance holds a resource (its constructor reads `{global}`); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}.{#field}`: {Class} instance has a private field (`{#field}` cannot be restored without running the constructor); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}`: {Class} extends `{Base}`, not a data class of this module (built-in and package bases keep state the browser cannot restore); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}`: {Class} is decorated (`{@decorator}` runs code when the class is constructed; the browser never constructs it); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
Cannot resume `{capture}.{field}`: {Class} field arrow reads `super` (it cannot run outside the class); create it inside the handler, build it with reconstruct(() => new {Class}(…)) or give {Class} a static [revive]
```

```text
RV2102: {Class} has [serialize] but no static [revive]
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

Create the instance where it is used (inside the handler or a clientEffect), build it with `reconstruct(() => new X(…))` from `@rivetjs/runtime/dom` (the browser runs the factory on first read), keep its data in signals, or give the class a `static [revive]` that rebuilds it in the browser.

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
class Conn { live = typeof window !== "undefined"; }
export function A() { const conn = new Conn(); return <b onClick={() => console.log(conn.live)}>x</b>; }
```

```tsx prefer
class Conn { live = typeof window !== "undefined"; }
export function A() { return <b onClick={() => console.log(new Conn().live)}>x</b>; }
```

## Quick fix

The [language service](../guides/tooling/language-service.md) (editor) and the MCP `check_code` tool offer this code action:

- Build it in the browser: `reconstruct(() => …)` → `const x = reconstruct(() => new X(…))`; reads become `x()` (+ import from @rivetjs/runtime/dom)

## When it is reported

Resume mode (Function Bridge T24). A data class declared at module scope of a resume module registers (`_rClass`) and its captured instances resume without running the constructor. Not eligible: an instance `#private` element or `accessor` field (no private brand without the constructor), a class or member decorator (runs code while constructing), a field arrow reading `super` / `new.target` (cannot run outside the class), an `extends` other than a data class of the same module (built-ins, packages, Node `EventEmitter`), a resource read while constructing (`window`, `document`, `navigator`, `globalThis`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `Worker`, `BroadcastChannel` in a field initializer or the constructor). Classes with an own or inherited `static [revive]` register as resource holders (T25): an instance with `[serialize]()` sends only that data and the browser rebuilds it with `static [revive](data)` on first use; package classes register the same hooks with `registerClass(cls, { id, serialize, revive })` from `@rivetjs/runtime/resume-format`. At render, `[serialize]` without `static [revive]` is `RV2102: {Class} has [serialize] but no static [revive]` (dev and production).
